Typhoon Champi's radius is around 320km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan.

FAST

TAIPEI: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday (Oct 23) ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi , which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, though the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kmh near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA). The storm was about 330km east of Taiwan's southern tip, the CWA said. The storm's forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan. The administration said its radius was around 320km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days.

Taiwan's financial markets will also close for Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal. The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with more than 350 international ones. In the capital Taipei, there were squally showers, but public transport, including the subway, was operating as usual, albeit with reduced service. Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too. The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan's westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.

Oct 23 : Oil prices were little changed in early Asian trade on Friday, after rising 4 per cent to a five-month high in the previous session due to concern of further energy supply disruption after Houthi attacks on top exporter Saudi Arabia. Brent crude futures was down 21 cents, or 0.2 per cent, at $112.96 a barrel as of 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 27 cents, or 0.3 per cent, at $98.12. On a weekly basis, WTI was on track to end two weeks of gain to finish lower. Brent, which settled at its highest since May 4 on Thursday, is set to close higher for the third successive week. Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters reported, as fighting intensified between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis.

Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognised government have raged since the Iran-aligned Houthis pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea. In Libya, an oil pipeline valve from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port has been shut, leading to a reduction in production at both fields, the head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday. Separately, Russia said on Wednesday it was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month, after President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoy Steve Witkoff for talks in St Petersburg. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he hoped negotiations, which would be the first since February, will take place early in November. Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, US energy data showed. Sanctions aimed at keeping Russian energy out of global markets after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 have pushed up oil prices.

SEOUL, Oct 23 : HD Hyundai Co said on Friday it has signed a deal with Kiewit Corp to start building an advanced US shipyard next year, with operations expected to begin in 2029 and create about 3,000 domestic jobs. The new shipyard is expected to boost US shipbuilding capacity and help revive the industry, Hyundai said. The partners will explore opportunities in both commercial ships and military support vessels, it said in a statement.  • South Korea pledged to invest $150 billion in the US shipbuilding sector, as part of $350 billion of investment funds the Asian country agreed to put into US projects in return for winning U.S. tariff cuts in last year. • Construction of the shipyard will begin in 2027 and the two companies will also set up a joint venture. • The joint venture will explore building US navy support vessels, commercial ship opportunities, and supplying ship blocks and modules to US shipyards. • HD Hyundai said the new shipyard is expected to revive the US shipbuilding industry and expand Korea-US shipbuilding cooperation.

FAST

Oct 22 : Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science. The model identifies and coordinates the questions that should be asked of a patient, as well as the exams and tests that should be ordered, using an "orchestrator" that organizes how AI will tackle a problem by employing a simulated panel of clinical experts collaborating to solve diagnostic cases, according to the report. Existing medical AI models typically take an all-at-once approach that examines all of a patient's symptoms, lab results and imaging studies to generate a diagnosis. With the orchestrator coordinating the steps to reaching a diagnosis, the AI model first decides what to ask about the patient’s history and what is significant in the physical exam. Based on what it learns, it decides which tests to order, considers the results, and orders further testing as appropriate.

All the while, it is updating its working hypotheses and plans, the research leaders said in an interview. Tasked with diagnosing more than 300 highly unusual and confusing medical dilemmas, the model employing the diagnostic orchestrator was more than twice as accurate at "working up" the patient and determining the diagnosis as general physicians using textbooks and the internet. The tool also outperformed human physicians when presented with scenarios drawn from a major database of emergency room admissions. Assessments comparing these types of older systems to human doctors usually use multiple-choice questions, the researchers said. "AI has become very good at getting a 100 per cent pass rate on those,” said Dr. Dominic King, the corporate vice president of the health unit at Microsoft AI, whose team is developing the new technology. “But of course, that's not real-world. No patient ever came to see me with a nice summary.” The researchers also found that diagnostic processes cost less when the orchestrator designs the work-ups than when human doctors do. “We're not just measuring the accuracy of the systems. We're also measuring how judiciously and carefully it goes through a diagnostic work-up,” said Harsha Nori, head of AI at Microsoft AI Health. In a collaboration with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, the researchers will next test the tool’s ability to triage patients in emergency department waiting rooms.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Oct 23 : Japan's manufacturing sector expanded at its slowest pace in seven months in October as output and new order growth eased, a business survey showed on Friday. • The flash S&P Global Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 53.3 in October from 54.1 in September. A reading above 50.0 indicates expansion in activity, while below that level signals contraction • New orders of goods producers rose at the weakest pace since March, while new export business across Japan's private sector increased at the softest rate in four months • Manufacturers logged the weakest rise in output since March, while goods producers recorded the slowest increase in new orders since March, the survey showed

FAST

Versatile actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Hollywood megahits including the sci-fi classic Alien, the war comedy M*A*S*H, and the action drama Top Gun, has died at the age of 93. Skerritt, a Detroit native whose Hollywood career spanned from the 1960s to the 2020s, died on Wednesday (Oct 21) of natural causes, his family said in a statement. "While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humour, curiosity, wisdom, generosity, and the love he brought into our lives," they said. "He cared deeply about imagination, creativity, storytelling, service, veterans, the natural world, and helping others find and share their own voices." Known for his rugged good looks and ability to shine in a variety of genres, Skerritt delivered memorable performances in leading and supporting roles in film and television. Skerritt's breakthrough role was a roguish US Army surgeon in director Robert Altman's 1970 Korean War black comedy M*A*S*H, a film whose ensemble cast also included Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould and Sally Kellerman. Skerritt played Southerner Duke Forrest as the doctors at the Mobile Army Surgical Hospital stitched up wounded troops. The film, whose popularity coincided with American unease over the Vietnam War, was nominated for five Academy Awards. In director Ridley Scott's claustrophobic 1979 sci-fi horror Alien, Skerritt played Dallas, the captain of an ill-fated spacecraft whose crew encounters a deadly parasitic extraterrestrial creature with a surrealist look and a bad attitude. In the film's famous and bloody "chestburster" scene, Skerritt's character is seated next to cast mate John Hurt when a baby alien violently exits the torso of Hurt's character. Alien, an influential masterpiece whose ensemble cast also included Sigourney Weaver and Ian Holm, earned two Oscar nominations. "It is spontaneity and impulse that make the difference, and that is what I felt we had with Alien. Every one of us had that immediate rapport with each other – the respect that I had for the other actors and the respect that they had for me," Skerritt told interviewer Peter Sobczynski in 2019, while also lauding Scott's directorial brilliance. Alien was one of several films in which Skerritt appeared that featured strong female characters, in this case Weaver's courageous character Ripley. That was considered pioneering at the time. "When I read the script, one of the things that I liked most about it was that the woman becomes the hero. I loved that," Skerritt said. "The sight of women being in positions of strength and fortitude to make the right connections and decisions was what appealed to me. I experienced that as well in Steel Magnolias, with the women in that. I liked the idea of women being tough and strong and influential." In Steel Magnolias (1989), Skerritt played Drum Eatenton, husband of Sally Field's M'Lynn Eatenton. Tony Scott, the brother of the Alien director, cast Skerritt in the key supporting role of naval aviation instructor Viper Metcalf in the 1986 blockbuster Top Gun that helped star Tom Cruise soar into Hollywood's stratosphere. Skerritt also played Shirley MacLaine's husband in director Herbert Ross's 1977 ballet drama The Turning Point, and starred alongside another emerging star in Brad Pitt in Robert Redford's beautifully shot 1992 period drama A River Runs Through It. Among other films in which he appeared were: Harold And Maude (1971), Ice Castles (1978), The Dead Zone (1983), Poltergeist III (1988), Contact (1997), Tears Of The Sun (2003) and Ted (2012). On the small screen, Skerritt starred in the offbeat CBS series Picket Fences from 1992 to 1996, playing a Wisconsin town sheriff and claiming an Emmy as outstanding lead actor in a drama series in 1993. Born on Aug 25, 1933, in Detroit, Skerritt served in the US Air Force before becoming an actor, making his film debut in 1962 alongside a young Redford in War Hunt. He was a father of five children and was married three times.

Source: Reuters/sr

TOKYO, Oct 23 : Japan has yet to see conditions met for the government to officially declare an end to deflation, Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said on Friday. The government's decision on whether to declare an end to deflation will take into account various factors to ensure Japan will not revert to periods of persistent price falls, Kiuchi told a press conference. Kiuchi made the remarks when asked by reporters about media reports the Bank of Japan may signal that underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2 per cent target at next week's policy meeting.

FAST

TOKYO, Oct 23 : Japan's annual core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2 per cent target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike. The figures underscored how higher fuel costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, elevated import prices driven by the weak yen and price pressures from robust AI demand were blunting the impact of government fuel subsidies. Having just raised interest rates last month, the Bank of Japan is set to stand pat on policy next week but may revise up its inflation forecast and signal its readiness to keep pushing up still-low borrowing costs, sources have told Reuters. The core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes volatile fresh food but includes fuel costs, rose 2.1 per cent in September from a year earlier, data showed, matching a median market forecast. It followed a 1.7 per cent rise in August.

An index that strips away the effects of both volatile fresh food and fuel, which is closely watched by the BOJ as a better gauge of demand-driven price pressures, rose 2.4 per cent in September from a year earlier after increasing 1.9 per cent in August. The BOJ raised its key rate to a 31-year high of 1.25 per cent last month, signalling a shift to guarding against underlying inflation overshooting its target and raising the prospect of additional rate hikes. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda has warned that underlying inflation, or the broad price trend stripping away temporary, one-off factors, may overshoot its 2 per cent target on price pressures from the Middle East conflict, a weak yen and brisk AI demand.

The Ferrari driver will be 42 in January and has a contract for 2027. Fernando Alonso, the oldest active F1 driver, is 45 and recently signed up for another season with Aston Martin. "I'm now forced to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa, and that's been my dream, to be able to race in Africa," Hamilton said at the US Grand Prix on Thursday in a press conference alongside championship leader Kimi Antonelli. "I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we'll keep it going."

Antonelli, who replaced Hamilton at Mercedes last season and is still only 20 years old, encouraged him: "You got to do at least the first one." Hamilton, the sport's first and only Black champion, has long campaigned for a race in Africa - a continent that last hosted a race at South Africa's Kyalami circuit in 1993 - and spoke of his efforts. "Countless meetings with the stakeholders, so many meetings with (F1 CEO) Stefano (Domenicali) at his office in London, but also on race weekends, countless calls: 'What's happening? Where are we going? Who are you meeting with?'  "Many meetings with different presidents from different countries. Lots of phone calls with different presidents from different countries within Africa," he recalled. "I think for me, it's a place that deserves to have a grand prix. It's about more than just one country. It's about the continent itself." Hamilton said an African race would make people more aware of the continent, but recognized there were concerns. Human rights campaigners Amnesty International recently accused Formula One of hollow words and offering Rwanda a "sportswashing prize" - an accusation leveled at countries perceived to be using sport to improve a tarnished image abroad. "Of course, I don't get to choose where we go. Naturally, there are problems all over the world today, so I've seen many of the stories. But I think we really have to approach it with humility," Hamilton said.  "Of course, going there doesn't mean that you neglect the things that are happening there. So hopefully many people start to educate themselves a little bit more about what is happening there and what has happened there for hundreds of years. I hope that does spark the conversation."

AUSTIN, Texas, Oct 22 : Lewis Hamilton had one piece of advice for Kimi Antonelli as the 20-year-old Mercedes driver stands on the verge of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion: "Slow down!" The Italian would have to win the US Grand Prix and have everything else fall his way for the title to be secured in Austin on Sunday but, with a lead of 102 points and a maximum 150 still to be won, he can be sure it is just a matter of time. Hamilton, winner of seven championships and the most successful driver in the history of the sport, left no doubt he was joking. "He doesn't need any advice. I think he's shown this year, and also last year, but particularly this year, his talent and his ability, his calmness and his approach," said the Ferrari driver of the man who replaced him at Mercedes last season.

"He's done an amazing job this year, and I'm so proud of him. I'm so proud of the way he's carried himself, how he interacts with the drivers and even with you guys," he told reporters on Thursday. "It's great to see him and the team excel. If it's not my team, I'd always want to see my old team do well." Antonelli would be the first Italian to take the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953 and, while professing to be taking one race at a time, he knows what awaits. "It definitely is crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," he said of the possibility that he could be champion already on Sunday with five races to spare as the calendar stands. "I've heard that something catastrophic needs to happen to the others for me to become champion (in Austin). For me, it needs to be a perfect weekend. The others need to have a poor result, which is unlikely to happen," he added. Antonelli said following in Hamilton's footsteps as a champion as well as a Mercedes driver would be a dream come true, but also made clear he was prepared to wait. "Obviously, I'm in an incredible position... But, of course, I still have to keep going, and the mindset is always the same: whenever I go on track, I want to be at the top and try to win as much as possible, whether I win the championship this weekend, next weekend or in Brazil. Let's see," he said.

(Refiles to add dropped words "unsolicited links" in SCAMMERS section) By AJ Vicens Oct 22 : Much of the world woke Wednesday to news that PHP, a coding language most people have never heard of but that underlies roughly 70 per cent of all websites, had a hackable vulnerability, sending businesses and governments scrambling to fix it. While the PHP glitches sit in the underlying code itself, the NSA warned that attackers could use them to take control of web servers to steal data, disrupt services or move through networks on services the average person relies on every day.

Experts say responsibility mostly lies with software providers and organizations that serve customers. But there are basic steps everyone should take to protect themselves.  USE MULTI-FACTOR AUTHENTIFICATION MFA, or multi-factor authentication, requires two forms of verification to access a protected site, such as a password plus a text-based code or security key. Emily Austin, principal security researcher at cybersecurity firm Censys, recommended unique passwords for individual websites, and for people to monitor any transactions. “But realistically, for situations like the PHP vulnerabilities, there really isn’t much an end user can do beyond hope the services they rely on either don’t use PHP or have people actively working on patching,” Austin said. The PHP flaws are the latest in a series of severe software bugs made worse by increasingly capable and accessible large language models. Long-hidden flaws in widely used software, once too obscure or complex for humans to exploit, are now much easier to surface and weaponize. MAKE HARDWARE UPDATES AUTOMATIC Dan Guido, CEO and co-founder of cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits, recommended people “turn on automatic updates for your phone, computer, and home router.” Companies typically issue security updates when patches are available for known vulnerabilities, so installing them promptly limits the window for bad actors.  Even so, consumers remain at the mercy of the services they rely on, Guido said. “Someone visiting a website can do everything right, like use two-factor authentication, and still have their information exposed,” Guido said. “You can't patch your hospital's website.”  Most of the work falls on companies running services, Guido said. “They need to deploy fixes faster and limit the damage that compromised systems can cause.” Runa Sandvik, the founder of Granitt and a digital security expert, said people need to update apps and services on their devices whenever they're available, and to not forget about internet-connected devices around the house. "I can see a scenario in which some people have some sort of IoT device at home that maybe doesn't get frequent updates, maybe doesn't get any updates at all," Sandvik said. "It's worth double checking with the vendor to see if there is anything available." PATCH, PATCH, PATCH Dr. Daniel Gardham, a lecturer at the Surrey Centre for Cyber Security and the University of Surrey, said organizations must know what software they run, patch promptly and check whether they've already been compromised. In the AI age, attackers have the advantage, Gardham added. “Finding vulnerabilities is becoming faster and easier, but fixing them across the range of systems that rely on this software is much harder,” Gardham said. “How well organizations manage that gap will determine whether AI makes the internet safer or more vulnerable.”  BEWARE OF SCAMMERS Any time a major cybersecurity threat makes the news, scammers and cybercriminals will try to take advantage, said Nic Adams, co-founder and CEO of 0rcus, a cyberkinetics company. Be wary of unsolicited links. "When these headlines hit, check the affected company's instructions by opening its app or typing its website address yourself," Adams said. "An urgent message telling you to 'secure your account' deserves extra scrutiny."  YOUR MONEY IS SAFE Banks have been preparing for this moment since frontier models came out, and have "worked extremely hard to ensure there is no more low-hanging fruit for the bad guys to go after," said Paul Benda, executive vice president of risk, fraud and cybersecurity at the American Bankers Association.  However, Benda added, "we are in a new normal" in terms of cyber threats, and consumers need to be aware, especially in the wake of the PHP vulnerabilities, when shopping with random retailers or websites "where their security is not going to be as good as your bank."  Benda said consumers should not reuse passwords across shopping sites, and should consider using passkeys where possible, which are digital keys specific to certain websites, that avoid the need to enter a password into a website and a phishing resistant.

Source: Reuters
